correctness.rationale: Every semigroup in the restricted multiplicity range has addition automatically closed below F; the exact word bijection and zero-run decomposition prove the two-parameter series including the ordinary boundary. Partial-fraction analysis has a unique simple dominant pole and the marked-pole derivative produces explicit positive variance. The uniformly summable geometric mixture proves independence. Sixteen exhaustive direct censuses, seventeen polynomial recurrence checks and five exact moment comparisons independently corroborate finite identities; none is mistaken for a proof of infinite asymptotics.

value.rationale: A natural and motivated infinite class (perfect semigroups at fixed Frobenius number) had previously been enumerated algorithmically rather than by a compact joint high-multiplicity formula. The exact bivariate census implies the parity-paired totals, sharp growth constant, positive-variance Gaussian genus limit and a nondegenerate independent geometric multiplicity boundary. These clarify typical arithmetic invariants and are not tiny numerical improvements, artificial slices, or a routine restatement.
